structured_output.summary: The change implements Date.prototype.toTimeString in its own file using existing helpers from crate::support::date. The steps run in spec order: this_time_value with `?` (covers RequireInternalSlot and the [[DateValue]] read), the NaN check returning "Invalid Date", LocalTime(tv), then TimeString(t) followed by TimeZoneString(tv), concatenated in that order. Errors propagate with `?`, nothing is special-cased, and no value is invented beyond the spec's "Invalid Date". I could not inspect the support::date helpers (this_time_value, local_time, time_string, time_zone_string) because they are outside the diff, so I did not verify that time_zone_string computes the real offset rather than returning a fixed string. The test262 gain (+4, 0 regressions) fits a change this size.
structured_output.notes_for_next_attempt: Non-blocking: the stub's spec comments were paraphrased rather than kept verbatim. The header line "This method performs the following steps when called:" was dropped, the names were changed to dateObj/tv/t instead of _dateObj_/_tv_/localTime, and step 2 became a parenthetical about thisTimeValue. CLAUDE.md asks for each step as a comment with the spec's text, so restoring the original comment text is preferable. Separately, check that support::date::time_zone_string derives the offset from the system time zone (SystemTimeZoneIdentifier / GetNamedTimeZoneOffsetNanoseconds) and does not hardcode UTC; that code is outside this diff.
